To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the budgetary system in schools is not designed to influence the strategic direction of schools.
budgeting in schools is largely determined by external forces, and that the link between budgeting and school strategy is loose.
The ERA did not result in a radical change in the nature of the budgeting and control process in schools.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between management control and the construction of budgets in schools.
the relationship between budgetary control and strategic management in schools.
the nature of budgetary control in schools and its impact upon the management of schools, particularly in terms of strategic management and the development of a corporate plan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there has been no clear link between budgetary control and strategic planning in the schools we have investigated.
budgeting and strategy in the schools we have studied are only loosely coupled, and that this relationship varies between schools.
there is no link between budgeting and school strategy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the budgeting process is largely concerned with the maintenance of a financial audit trail, with little attention paid to the strategic implications of expenditure.
the ERA has not had a major impact upon the nature of budgeting and planning in schools.
the introduction of the delegated budget has not had any significant effect upon the nature of management control in schools.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are significant differences in the extent to which schools are able to develop strategic plans and budgets.
budgetary control is not an adequate means of influencing school strategy, although it may have other uses.
the ERA 1988 did not have the effect of increasing the strategic role of school budgets.
